title: Mirabel and the Bakery
premise: Casper Underhill, a jaded wedding planner in the seaside town of Gullwick, has spent ten years anonymously writing letters to a stranger he met one summer—letters signed only 'the Bakery,' named for the shuttered shop where they first talked. When the letters' recipient, Mirabel Quill, moves in next door to reopen that very bakery, Casper must hide his identity while planning the high-society wedding that will demolish her bakery and the harbor cottages. As the wedding approaches and the last ferry of the season nears departure, Casper's employer—the groom's ruthless father—threatens everything Mirabel has built. In the end, Casper sacrifices his career and confesses his decade of letters, and Mirabel, choosing truth over the safe life waiting across the water, stays after the last train leaves, reopening the bakery as their own.
about_author: Ivo Blackwood is the pen name of a former pastry chef turned novelist who lives in a coastal village and writes love stories about people who arrive too late. This is their third novel, all set in fictional seaside towns where the tide keeps everyone's secrets.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Season
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper arrives in Gullwick to plan the Ashcombe wedding, the biggest contract of his career, and privately marks the calendar: last ferry, October 14th. He writes his tenth anniversary letter and burns it instead of sending. Emotional beat: ritualized grief disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Flour on the Fence Line
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel inherits her late aunt's bakery and cottage next door to a curt neighbor who won't give his name. She finds a decades-old letter wedged in the bakery wall, signed 'the Bakery.' Emotional beat: cautious hope; she decides to stay through the season.

chapters.title: A Man Who Plans Endings
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper realizes his new neighbor is the bakery's new owner—Mirabel Quill, the girl from that summer. He lies about his name, calling himself 'Cass.' Emotional beat: panic and self-loathing; the past tense collapses.

chapters.title: Sourdough and Small Talk
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel charms her gruff neighbor into tasting her first loaves; he critiques them like a man who knows her aunt's recipes. She notices he flinches at the word 'wedding.' Emotional beat: warmth cracking his shell.

chapters.title: The Ashcombe Brief
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper's client, Edmund Ashcombe, reveals the wedding venue requires demolishing the harbor cottages—including the bakery—for a private lawn. Casper signs anyway, telling himself it's just business. Emotional beat: complicity; the first real corruption of his conscience.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Signed
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel tells Cass about 'the Bakery,' her decade of anonymous letters and the one summer she's never gotten over. Casper, holding his breath, learns she kept every letter. Emotional beat: agonizing near-confession; intimacy built on a lie.

chapters.title: Tasting Cake for a Lie
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Mirabel caters the wedding tasting; Casper watches Edmund humiliate her and says nothing. That night he writes a letter to her, unsigned, and leaves it in her mailbox. Emotional beat: guilt finding its only honest channel.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Correspondent
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel receives the letter and recognizes the voice—identical to the old letters. She begins leaving replies in the bakery's old dumbwaiter, addressed to 'the Bakery.' Emotional beat: falling for a ghost while her living neighbor grows dearer.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Man
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper lives a double life: daytime Cass the neighbor, midnight the Bakery the letter-writer, and all the while the demolition order creeps closer. He starts sabotaging the wedding timeline in small ways. Emotional beat: the saboteur's thrill and terror.

chapters.title: What Edmund Wants
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Edmund Ashcombe offers Mirabel triple value to sell early; she refuses. He hints he knows something about her 'pen pal' that she doesn't. Emotional beat: menace; power showing its teeth.

chapters.title: The Storm Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A storm cancels the rehearsal dinner; Casper and Mirabel shelter in the bakery, baking bread by lamplight. He almost tells her everything; instead he kisses her. Emotional beat: the lie and the truth colliding at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Dark
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel, elated and uneasy, finds Casper's dropped planner—his real name inside, and the demolition schedule. She says nothing, testing him. Emotional beat: the first crack of betrayal, loyalty vs. truth beginning to split.

chapters.title: The Ferry Timetable
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Edmund discovers the sabotage and threatens to expose Casper's anonymous letters as harassment, plus the fraud of his false name. He gives Casper a deadline: deliver Mirabel's signature or lose everything. Emotional beat: cornered; duty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: What the Dumbwaiter Said
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel finds Casper's final unsigned letter hidden in the dumbwaiter—a full confession of the summer, the decade, the name. She confronts him at his door; he can't deny it. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the cruelest truth is the kindest one.

chapters.title: Silence Between Loaves
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Mirabel cuts him off completely. Casper, hollowed out, nearly signs the demolition papers and takes the ferry out. Emotional beat: rock bottom; the man who plans endings planning his own.

chapters.title: The Bakers' Petition
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel rallies the harbor families to fight the demolition, discovering Casper's sabotage delayed it by weeks—evidence he fought for her. She reads his ten years of letters again, all of them, and weeps. Emotional beat: anger transmuting into understanding.

chapters.title: Confession at the Register
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper walks into Edmund's office and resigns publicly, surrendering the Ashcombe contract and his reputation, then posts the true story of the letters and the land grab to the whole town. Emotional beat: sacrifice; truth finally outranking loyalty to a corrupt employer.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The Ashcombe wedding collapses as the bride, learning of the demolition, walks out; Edmund's power crumbles. Mirabel watches Casper take the blame for everything on the town square. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by fear he'll leave on the last ferry.

chapters.title: Last Train, First Truth
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper, ruined and certain Mirabel will never forgive him, buys a ticket on the last train out before the ferry. At the platform, he finds a fresh loaf and a letter in the dumbwaiter style: 'Stay after the last train. I'll be at the bakery.' Emotional beat: the choice the whole book has turned on.

chapters.title: The Ferry Departs Without Him
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel waits in the bakery as the ferry horn sounds across the harbor, terrified she's misread everything. The door opens. Casper, soaked, carrying nothing but a letter he wrote her ten years ago. Emotional beat: the leap of faith landing.

chapters.title: What the Bakery Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They read the decade of letters aloud to each other through the night, baking as they go—grief, apology, and the summer finally spoken in present tense. Emotional beat: reconciliation; love against duty, duty having lost.

chapters.title: Opening Day
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Casper's shared POV. Spring: the bakery reopens with a new sign—'Underhill & Quill'—and the harbor cottages stand saved. Casper plans one last event: not a wedding, but an opening, and asks Mirabel to stay in every tense. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy; the letters end because the letters are no longer needed.
